purpose: final-benchmark landscape research (user asked for alternatives to SWE-bench Verified); constraints: official protocol only, machine Docker currently broken, 9B student, training pools = Klear-66k(SWE-smith)/SWE-Gym/R2E, frozen subsets allowed
key_finding: ALL agentic SWE benchmarks grade via Docker/container harnesses (SWE-bench family, SWE-bench-Live, SWE-rebench fork, Multi-SWE-bench, SWE-bench Pro, Terminal-Bench/Harbor). Switching benchmarks does NOT escape the Docker platform gap; it only changes contamination story and comparability.

candidates.name: SWE-bench Verified
candidates.citation: Jimenez et al., SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?, arXiv 2310.06770; Verified split by OpenAI 2024
candidates.pros: field default - every project we cite reports it (DeepSWE 59.0, AgentForge 39.4, Polar 26.4, Qwen3CN 70.6-71.3, GLM-5 TR rows); our exclusion audit already covers its 500 ids
candidates.cons: OpenAI publicly stopped using it: 'increasingly contaminated and mismeasures frontier coding progress' (openai.com/index/why-we-no-longer-evaluate-swe-bench-verified); SWE-MERA reports 32.67% of successful patches involve direct solution memorization (arXiv 2507.11059)

candidates.name: SWE-rebench V2
candidates.citation: Badertdinov, Nekrashevich, Shevtsov, Golubev (Nebius): SWE-rebench arXiv 2505.20411 (NeurIPS 2025 D&B, ~138 cites); V2 arXiv 2602.23866 (ICML 2026)
candidates.tasks: V2: 32,079 executable tasks, 20 languages, 3,617 repos, pre-built images; +120k extended; V1 continuously decontaminated (removes future-commit leak vectors, e.g. Claude Code reading git history)
candidates.harness: github.com/SWE-rebench/SWE-bench-fork (SWE-bench fork, container-based F2P<=50 + P2P validation)
candidates.pros: DATA ALREADY DOWNLOADED LOCALLY (data/raw/nebius__SWE-rebench-V2); decontaminated-by-design answers the SV contamination criticism; continuous updates resist training-set leakage
candidates.cons: harness is still container-based; V2 abstract mentions F2P but no P2P on extended set

candidates.name: SWE-bench-Live
candidates.citation: Linghao Zhang et al. (Microsoft): SWE-bench Goes Live!, arXiv 2505.23419 (NeurIPS 2025 D&B, ~108 cites)
candidates.tasks: 1,890 tasks / 223 repos (initial 1,319), issues created since 2024, rolling weekly updates, multi-language multi-OS
candidates.harness: github.com/microsoft/swe-bench-live, evaluation/ dir, per-task executable Docker sandbox; also offers task-creation code for agentic RFT/RL
candidates.pros: Microsoft-backed, live-updating, substantial perf gap vs static benches documented; RL task-creation tooling aligns with our stage-2 needs
candidates.cons: Docker; data not yet local; newer, fewer third-party baselines to compare against

candidates.name: SWE-bench Pro
candidates.citation: Scale AI: SWE-Bench Pro: Can AI Agents Solve Long-Horizon Software Engineering Tasks?, arXiv 2509.16941 (~206 cites)
candidates.tasks: 1,865 long-horizon instances; public subset 11 repos + held-out 12 repos (commercial)
candidates.pros: OpenAI's recommended SV replacement; held-out set resists contamination
candidates.cons: frontier-difficulty - public leaderboard is frontier-model territory, a 9B on 2-4 cards likely scores ~0; held-out portion not runnable by us

candidates.name: Multi-SWE-bench
candidates.cons: our student/pools are Python-centric - mismatch for now

candidates.name: Terminal-Bench (2.0->4.0)
candidates.citation: Laude Institute + Stanford + community: Terminal-Bench: Benchmarking Agents on Hard, Realistic Tasks, arXiv 2601.11868
candidates.tasks: 89 hard human-verified terminal tasks (2.0), version 4.0 current
candidates.pros: terminal-mastery axis complements repo-repair; GLM-5 TR environment layer is Harbor-format (already relevant to our stack)
candidates.cons: different task shape than SWE repair; Docker

candidates.name: LiveSWEBench
candidates.tasks: real-world tasks for end-user assistant APPLICATIONS (Cursor-class), 3 task types, seniority levels
candidates.cons: evaluates products, not raw models+harness - not our shape

candidates.name: evalplus (official CLI, full protocol)
candidates.tasks: function-level; full plus_input harness beyond our base-check
candidates.harness: pip evalplus, runs locally, NO DOCKER
candidates.pros: immediately runnable today; upgrades our guardrail from base-check (32) to an official evalplus score; LiveCodeBench also Docker-free if a contamination-free function-level row is wanted

recommendation: PRIMARY: SWE-bench Verified frozen subset (comparability with all cited prior art; exclusion audit already done) - Docker platform fix remains the prerequisite
SECONDARY: SWE-rebench (data already local; decontaminated-by-design; hedge against the contamination criticism OpenAI raised) - same Docker prerequisite
IMMEDIATE: official evalplus CLI for the function-level guardrail row (no Docker, runnable today)
SWE-bench-Live noted as optional third if we later want Microsoft's live set or its RL task-creation tooling for stage 2
